context: 2026-11-14 done. https://github.com/BenchBox-dev/benchbox/pull/4234 (merge 949f560, oracle SHIP, required checks green) gives docs/agent/batch-tracker-contract.md one ordered runtime-move sequence: stop every session and MCP server on the old runtime, run `uv sync --project _project/scripts --locked --dry-run`, then the real (exact) sync in the primary clone, then restart; it says never to sync while a session still uses the old runtime. description:
Gap. Tracker entry points run `uv run --project _project/scripts --locked -- ...`, which installs what the lock needs but never removes extras. On 2026-11-12 the primary clone's _project/scripts/.venv still held todo_db 0.15.0 next to tractable 1.1.1. todo_db had been BenchBox's runtime until #4013 merged on 2026-11-07, so it lingered for five days and two runtime moves. A venv that does not match uv.lock lets a stale import of a retired package succeed locally while it fails in CI and in fresh worktrees. By 2026-11-14 the venv had been synced: `uv sync --project _project/scripts --locked --dry-run` in the primary reports "Would make no changes".

Decision (owner, 2026-11-14): add one step to the documented runtime-move procedure. After the move lands and every session on the old runtime has restarted, run `uv sync --project _project/scripts --locked` (exact by default) in the primary clone, checking first with --dry-run. No change to the uv run calls.

Guardrails:
- The step is an owner step in the primary clone; agents keep no write path there.
- It runs only after sessions on the old runtime have restarted, so no running server loses a package it imports.
- uv.lock is not changed.
